Perturbing snap.bid_size_1 moved l1_imbalance, total_bid_depth, depth_imbalance, book_slope_bid and others. The equality check FIRED, so it is capable of detecting a corrupted adapter.

why_a_record_and_not_an_assertion: A stranger cloning this repository sees '39 passed, 4 skipped' and cannot tell whether those four have ever passed or how to run them. A skip marker keeps a test runnable; it does not stand in for having run it. This file is the checkable part.

run_2026_09_03.why_this_run_happened: DELTA R212 section 5 asked what the four skips in every reported suite line actually are. They are these, gated on LEAKAUDIT_FIXTURE=1 for cost. Running them was the answer, and it turned up that this record had gone stale AGAIN by the same mechanism its own banner describes: the 2026-09-02 entry attests commit 8320a20, and src/leakaudit/availability.py has been changed by four commits since. The banner warned about twelve such commits last time; nothing detected the recurrence.
run_2026_09_03.the_gap_this_run_exposed: `test_every_opt_in_test_has_a_recorded_result` runs in the DEFAULT suite and passed throughout the stale period. It checks that every opt-in test HAS a recorded result. It does not check that the result is CURRENT. So the always-run guard cannot see the failure mode this file was written to warn about, and the warning is carried by a prose banner that no test reads.
run_2026_09_03.attests_method: sha256 per module, over the modules these tests EXECUTED, measured in-process with probe_path_guard.record_modules(). Currency is a digest comparison, not commit ancestry: it fires when something that could change the answer changed, and stays quiet otherwise.
run_2026_09_03.SUPERSEDED_CLAIM_read_this_with_the_two_: The fields `why_this_run_happened` and `the_gap_this_run_exposed` below assert that this record had gone stale again. THAT IS FALSE and is corrected in `correction_2026_09_03`. They are kept because they are what was believed and written, and because the shape of the error -- a module name carried from one finding into another without checking whether the changed module was the guarded module -- is the useful part.

correction_2026_09_03.what_is_false: That this record had gone stale again. It had gone COMMIT-stale: it cited an older commit. It had never gone CONTENT-stale.
correction_2026_09_03.the_measurement_that_settles_it: The modules these tests EXECUTE were measured rather than assumed: fixture_adapter.py, determinism.py, evidence/fixture_spike/f2/fixture.py and phase5_ml_fixture.py. Every one is byte-identical to the code attested at 8320a20. `availability.py`, whose four changes prompted the false finding, is not among them.
correction_2026_09_03.the_count_that_matters: ZERO. No content-staleness has occurred, so tools/opt_in_currency.py has zero demonstrated true positives. Any description of it as built after a defect that bit twice describes a history that did not happen.
correction_2026_09_03.what_the_episode_IS_evidence_for: Keying currency to content rather than to commit ancestry. The ruling against ancestry was made on the argument that it fires on unrelated changes; its first application turned a twice-reported finding into a twice-made false positive, so the failure mode was not hypothetical.

run_2026_09_03.staleness_trigger: This module set was MEASURED AT ONE COMMIT by running the opt-in tests in-process under probe_path_guard.record_modules(). A structural change to what these tests execute -- a new module in the adapter's path, or the fixture's producing code reorganised -- requires re-measuring it with `python tools/opt_in_currency.py --measure <run_key>`. The digests below detect a CHANGE to a recorded module; they cannot detect a NEW module that was never recorded, which is what re-measuring is for.
run_2026_09_03.why_the_totality_test_pattern_is_NOT_use: PROBE_PATH_SET.json is checked for totality: its on-path and off-path lists are disjoint and together cover every module in the package, so a new module lands in neither and fails. That pattern does not fit this set. It is a measured execution trace with no complementary 'known not to execute' list, and the universe it would have to cover -- the package plus the fixture's producing code -- is not a set anyone has a reason to classify exhaustively for this question. What stands in for it: a test asserts the attested set is non-empty and names the adapter, so an empty or unmeasured block cannot read as current, and a second asserts this set and the probe's are disjoint, so if the two questions ever merge somebody rewrites that assertion rather than deleting it.
